tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
- The recorded session navigated to Magento admin orders grid, logged in, closed a popup, filled filters (order # and billing name), tried selecting store and status, clicked Search, exported CSV, used mass-action, selected a row, and opened the order view to extract details. Several attempts to select the Store filter failed; logs recommend using attribute-based XPaths and waiting for loading overlays.

Task Definition:
- Create a reusable, deterministic tool that: navigates to the admin orders grid, applies filter inputs (order number, billing name, date ranges, GT ranges, store, status), triggers search, optionally exports results, selects the first row and executes a mass-action, and optionally opens the first matching order View and extracts structured order details.

Action Plan:
1. Navigate to {base_url}/sales_order/ (start point). 2. Wait for page/loaders. 3. Fill all filter inputs (write empty string when parameter not provided). 4. Use attribute-based selects/XPaths for store and status. 5. Click Search (last filter cell button). 6. Wait for grid reload. 7. Extract visible orders into 'orders'. 8. If export_format provided, select it and click Export. 9. Select first-row checkbox. 10. Choose massaction and click Submit. 11. Wait and extract mass action results. 12. Extract first View href, navigate to it and extract order details.

Variable Identification (inputs):
- base_url: root admin URL used to construct navigation target. Required to allow different installations.
- increment_id: order # filter (input[name='increment_id']). Optional.
- billing_name: billing name filter (input[name='billing_name']). Optional.
- created_at_from / created_at_to: date-range filters. Optional.
- gt_base_from / gt_base_to / gt_purchased_from / gt_purchased_to: numeric range filters. Optional.
- store: visible option text for Purchased From (Store) filter (e.g., 'English'). Optional.
- status: visible option text for Status filter (e.g., 'Pending'). Optional.
- export_format: CSV/Excel/XML to trigger export. Optional.
- massaction: visible text for Actions dropdown (e.g., 'Print Invoices'). Optional.
- open_first_match: 'true' or 'false' to open first result page and extract details. Optional (default true recommended).

Step Optimization:
- Use table header-scoped XPaths (thead tr[2] filter row and tbody tr[1]) and core Magento input names where available (increment_id, created_at[from]/[to], billing_name, shipping_name, status, order_ids[]). This is more robust than counting global tabbable indices (the previous attempt produced strict-mode violations). 
- Use attribute-based selectors (select[name*='store'] and select[name='status']) with header-text fallbacks to fix the repeated 'could not select store' failures.
- Insert waits after operations that trigger AJAX and recommend waiting for #loading-mask invisibility if the runner supports visibility checks. Where conditional waiting isn't available use conservative wait seconds (2-3s) as included.
- For View navigation prefer reading the anchor href and navigating directly (driver.get(href)) rather than relying on click() to avoid JS interceptors or preventedDefault handlers.

Notes and constraints:
- The tool assumes an authenticated admin session is already present. Do not include authentication steps.
- Steps intentionally write empty strings into inputs when parameters are omitted so the sequence remains deterministic and re-executable without conditional branching.
- If the environment does not support reading outputs as {first_view_href[0].view_href}, callers should use the 'orders' extract output to pick a view href and call the navigation step separately.

Overall: This tool provides a deterministic, attribute-driven automation sequence that reproduces the recorded browser session and includes fixes for the store-select instability and loader handling observed in earlier failures.
name: magento_admin_orders_tool
description: Automate searching and operating on Magento 1.x admin Orders grid (fill filters, search, export, mass-action, open order view and extract details). Assumes the browser session is already authenticated in the admin.

steps.description: Navigate to the Magento Orders grid page.
Wait for the page and any initial loaders to appear; give JS time to initialize (if enabled).
Extra wait to allow #loading-mask/ajax-loader to settle before interacting. Automation should additionally check for #loading-mask invisibility if supported by the runner.
Set Order # filter (input[name='increment_id']). If {increment_id} is empty this writes an empty value.
Set Billing name filter (input[name='billing_name']). If {billing_name} empty, writes empty value.
Set Purchased On 'From' date filter (created_at[from]). Write empty string if not provided.
Set Purchased On 'To' date filter (created_at[to]). Write empty string if not provided.
Set G.T. (Base) From value. Leave empty to skip.
Set G.T. (Base) To value. Leave empty to skip.
Set G.T. (Purchased) From value. Leave empty to skip.
Set G.T. (Purchased) To value. Leave empty to skip.
Select the Purchased From (Store) filter by visible option text. Uses attribute-based select[name*='store'] first, with header-scoped XPath fallback.
Select the Status filter by visible option text (select[name='status']).
Click the Search button in the filter row (last filter cell).
Wait for grid to reload and for any loading-mask/ajax-loader to finish.
Capture first page of matching order rows and their view hrefs into 'orders' output.
steps.goal: Extract matching orders: order_number, store, purchased_on, bill_to_name, ship_to_name, grand_total(s), status, and view link hrefs for visible rows

steps.description: If {export_format} is provided (CSV/Excel/XML), select that export type in the Export control. If the export control is implemented as links instead of a select, the next click steps will still attempt to trigger Export via its button/link.
Click the Export control/button or the appropriate CSV/Excel/XML link to trigger export (if export_format was chosen).
Wait for export action to start/complete (server-driven download or AJAX).
Select the first visible row's checkbox to prepare for a mass-action.
Choose a mass-action from the Actions dropdown (choose by visible text).
Click the mass-action Submit button to apply the selected action to selected rows.
Wait for mass-action to complete and any messages to appear.
Extract any messages displayed after executing the mass-action and the current grid state (selected count, visible rows).
steps.goal: Capture mass-action messages and updated grid state (e.g., messages shown in the header and selected items count)

steps.description: Extract the href of the first 'View' anchor (a[href*='/admin/sales_order/view/order_id/']) to allow direct navigation to the order view page.
steps.goal: Locate first visible View link href (if present) into 'first_view_href' to allow direct navigation

steps.description: Navigate directly to the first matching order's view page using the captured view href. If {open_first_match} is 'false' or no first_view_href present, this navigation may attempt to navigate to an empty URL; calling system should set open_first_match='true' to enable.
Wait for order view page to load.
Capture structured order details from the order view page.
steps.goal: Extract order details from the order view: order number, admin order id, status, date, customer (name,email), billing/shipping addresses, payment & shipping methods, items (sku,name,qty,price,row_total), and totals

input_schema.name: base_url
input_schema.description: Base admin URL (omit trailing slash). Example: "http://dockerized-magento.local/index.php/admin"

input_schema.name: increment_id
input_schema.description: Order number / increment id to filter (input[name='increment_id']). Leave empty to skip narrowing by order number.

input_schema.name: billing_name
input_schema.description: Billing name free-text filter (input[name='billing_name']). Leave empty to skip.

input_schema.name: created_at_from
input_schema.description: Purchased On - From date (created_at[from]) in MM/DD/YYYY format.

input_schema.name: created_at_to
input_schema.description: Purchased On - To date (created_at[to]) in MM/DD/YYYY format.

input_schema.name: gt_base_from
input_schema.description: G.T. (Base) - From numeric filter. Leave empty to skip.

input_schema.name: gt_base_to
input_schema.description: G.T. (Base) - To numeric filter. Leave empty to skip.

input_schema.name: gt_purchased_from
input_schema.description: G.T. (Purchased) - From numeric filter. Leave empty to skip.

input_schema.name: gt_purchased_to
input_schema.description: G.T. (Purchased) - To numeric filter. Leave empty to skip.

input_schema.name: store
input_schema.description: Store view option text, e.g. "English" (matches visible option text in Purchased From (Store) filter).

input_schema.name: status
input_schema.description: Order status option text to select from the Status dropdown, e.g. "Pending". Leave empty to skip.

input_schema.name: export_format
input_schema.description: Export format to trigger after search. Choose one of CSV, Excel, or XML. Leave empty to skip export.

input_schema.name: massaction
input_schema.description: Mass-action option visible text to apply (e.g. "Print Invoices"). Use exact visible text of the action as shown in the Actions dropdown. Leave empty to skip mass-action.

input_schema.name: open_first_match
input_schema.description: If set to 'true', the tool will open the first matching order's View page and extract order details. Use 'true' or 'false'. Default: 'true'.
